answer.answer: Northstar did not remove policy checks; they were renamed. The Northstar 3 guide documents that 'Northstar 3 calls pre-deployment controls policy checks' [northstar-policy-old]. The Northstar 4 migration guide states that 'Northstar 4 renames policy checks to release guards; their purpose is unchanged' [northstar-policy-new]. So the controls persist under a new name ('release guards') with the same purpose. What remains historically valid: the term 'policy checks' was the Northstar 3 name for pre-deployment controls [northstar-policy-old]. Unresolved: any behavioral differences beyond the rename and the detailed mechanics/scope of these controls are not documented in the supplied sources.
change_events: Northstar 4 renames 'policy checks' to 'release guards'; their purpose is unchanged [northstar-policy-new].
current_truths: In Northstar 4, pre-deployment controls are called 'release guards' [northstar-policy-new].
The purpose of these controls is unchanged by the rename [northstar-policy-new].
historical_truths: In Northstar 3, pre-deployment controls were called 'policy checks' [northstar-policy-old].
